facts.raw_span: bilateral ventriculomegaly with dilation of both frontal and occipital horns
multiple hyperechoic regions with indistinct margins within the ventricular lumens
areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles

a comprehensive workup—including a TORCH panel, platelet count, prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time, plasminogen levels, von Willebrand factor, factor V Leiden, protein S, protein C, and antiplatelet antibodies—returned within normal limits

concepts.why: Bilateral ventriculomegaly and ventricular enlargement are indicative of congenital hydrocephalus
Bilateral ventriculomegaly with irregular ventricular walls and hyperechoic regions suggests fetal ventriculomegaly
Although the TORCH panel was normal, intrauterine infection is a possible cause of fetal ventriculomegaly
The comprehensive workup included coagulation studies, which were normal, but fetal coagulopathy is a possible cause of fetal ventriculomegaly
Bilateral ventriculomegaly and a roughened-appearing choroid plexus suggest a CNS anomaly
Bilateral ventricular enlargement and areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images suggest a fetal brain anomaly

rationales.F05: Bilateral ventriculomegaly is a key feature of Congenital Hydrocephalus and Fetal Ventriculomegaly.
rationales.F10: Bilateral ventricular enlargement is a key feature of Congenital Hydrocephalus and Fetal Ventriculomegaly.
rationales.F12: Normal comprehensive workup results rule out Intrauterine Infection and Fetal Coagulopathy.
